Solution 1 is correct. Since $f(2)=6$, we have $f^{-1}(6)=2$. Since $f(1)=2$, we have $f^{-1}(2)=1$. So $f^{-1}(f^{-1}(6))=1$.

Solution 2 misreads $f^{-1}(2)$ as $f(2)$. Solution 3 invents a linear model for $f^{-1}$ from two points, which the problem does not support, and its answer of 10 is wrong.

CHOICE: 1
